items.text: Great speaking with @SBUPrez Maurie McInnis yesterday about the University's programing and efforts that benefit Long Island. Stony Brook is a center of innovation for both healthcare and education and I'm glad to be able to continue to support them in Congress. https://t.co/kvWzDSglRk

If Congress does not act quickly to address the program's impending funding shortfall, then the men and women who put their lives on the line and who survived the 9/11 terrorist attacks could lose health coverage as soon as 2024. 

We cannot allow that to happen.

I voted to expand access to over-the-counter contraception and am a cosponsor of @RepBice’s bill safeguarding contraceptives while also preserving healthcare provider conscience protections. These are better alternatives to the partisan bill Democrats pushed through today.

There should be no room for the Chinese government to unilaterally exercise law enforcement on U.S. soil. That's why last week I joined @RepAshleyHinson in urging the Administration to act on this disturbing report of CCP police presence in New York.

https://t.co/21AamJCOVm

Chuck Schumer repeatedly promised that 9/11 healthcare would be prioritized in the Senate this year and now, at the 11th hour, he has pulled the rug out from under 9/11 families. They deserve better than to have been lied to by Democrat leadership for the last two years...(2/3)

I intro'd The Metastatic Breast Cancer Access to Care Act with @USRepKCastor so those with metastatic breast cancer can gain immediate access to SSDI & Medicare benefits. This bill would offer financial relief to patients so they can focus on what's most important, fighting back. https://t.co/SlpKAByMk6

Today, I introduced the bipartisan bicameral 9/11 Responder and Survivor Health Funding Correction Act of 2023 alongside @SenGillibrand to close the @WTCHealthPrgm funding gap and safeguard 9/11 responder and survivors' access to healthcare for 9/11 related illnesses. https://t.co/QLbh4izsRx

Today, the WTCHP provides healthcare for 120,000+ first responders and survivors, spanning every state and all but one congressional district. But, at a time when more Americans than ever before are suffering from 9/11 related illnesses, the program is facing a funding shortage.

We made a promise to #NeverForget. That's why this week I announced the 9/11 Responder and Survivor Health Funding Correction Act to close the @WTCHealthPrgm funding gap and ensure our 9/11 survivors and first responders continue to have access to the healthcare they deserve. https://t.co/y47vdiBHNn

The NYS DOH has issued an Air Quality Health Advisory, including for LI and NYC. All New Yorkers, but especially higher risk individuals, should take steps to reduce their exposure. Click here to learn how and to to track air quality near you⬇️ https://t.co/ex3AzZPJbG

22 yrs after 9/11, Americans are still getting sick from 9/11-related illnesses. Now, their access to the health care they were promised is at risk. It’s time to deliver on our promise to never forget by closing the funding gap in the WTCHP. Read more⬇️ https://t.co/L6JPAkE3DT

The devastation of 9/11 is far from behind us. First responders and survivors are still getting sick from 9/11-related illnesses. I and other NYers in Congress will continue fighting to ensure our 9/11 heroes retain access to the health care they need. 
https://t.co/reyfwBZCeK

This week, I reintroduced the Veteran Suicide Prevention Act. It's unthinkable that so many American heroes are losing their lives to suicide after surviving the horrors of war. We must take action to safeguard our veterans' mental health. https://t.co/rreEtFL5cD

Whether it’s Superstorm Sandy or flash flooding due to rain like we saw yesterday, we know that flood insurance is essential for Long Island homeowners. I am fighting to ensure the NFIP doesn’t lapse so Long      Islanders aren't left without protection.

This week, @RepGonzalez and I led 20 of our colleagues in sending a letter to @FEMA Administrator Deanne Criswell urging more affordable flood insurance payment options for NFIP policyholders. 

Read our letter below⬇️ https://t.co/JqjifyT51m

I will always fight to ensure all those impacted by 9/11-related illnesses have access to the health care they need.

I am proud to have recently secured critical funding for the @WTCHealthPrgm.

More than two decades after 9/11, tens of thousands of first responders and survivors are still suffering from 9/11-related illnesses.

It's for them that we must #NeverForget and it's for them that I am leading the fight to fully fund the World Trade Center Health Program.

Today, more than 132,000 Americans are enrolled in the World Trade Center Health Program. 

Learn more about our fight to safeguard access to health care for 9/11 responders and survivors: https://t.co/KkWzEYuQDg https://t.co/xpttzs3mk3

Every person suffering from 9/11-related illnesses deserves to have access to the health care they need. That's why I am proud to have helped ensure that excluded 9/11 responders to the Pentagon & Shanksville can participate in the WTCHP starting TODAY. ⬇ https://t.co/ObOfN2h4Bw
